The Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, India, with a capacity of 132,000, is the largest cricket stadium in the world.

Picture by Reuters

By Rahul Venkat

24 February 2021 12:41 GMT+0 3 min read

The **world’s biggest cricket stadium** – the Narendra Modi Stadium in the Motera area of Ahmedabad -- is a refurbished stadium – earlier known as the Sardar Patel Stadium. It was inaugurated in 2020 and has the capacity to hold 132,000 spectators, making it the biggest cricketing venue ever.

Overall, it sits second behind the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, which is the **biggest stadium in the world** , with a capacity of 150,000 .

Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad holds 132,000 spectators, which makes it not only the world’s largest cricket stadium but the world’s largest stadium of any kind. It opened in its current rebuilt form in 2020, replacing the older Sardar Patel Stadium that occupied the same site since 1982. The complete rebuild was driven by the Gujarat Cricket Association at a cost of around $114 million, and the result is a venue that genuinely changes how you think about what “big” means for a sports facility.

The architecture is striking. A modern oval bowl with two tiers all the way around, an LED-illuminated exterior, four dressing rooms that can host two simultaneous matches, and a 55-meter-wide playing field. When it’s full for an India vs Pakistan cricket match, the noise level is documented to rival anything in football.

The stadium was originally built for the 13th World Festival of Youth and Students, and its scalloped roof design (16 arches meant to resemble a magnolia blossom) is genuinely striking.

Here’s what makes it strange, though. Rungrado isn’t really used as a sports venue anymore. It hosts the Mass Games, North Korea’s massive choreographed propaganda spectacle, and the occasional political rally. Satellite imagery suggests it’s gone through periods of disrepair. Football matches have been played there, but irregularly.

So yes, it’s technically the second-largest stadium in the world and the largest football venue. But it’s also arguably the least accessible and least active stadium on this entire list. Make of that what you will.

What’s wild about Michigan Stadium is how it achieves its size. The bowl sits mostly below ground level, so from the outside, it doesn’t look nearly as massive as it is. You walk in at what feels like ground level and realize you’re standing near the top of the upper deck. It’s a clever bit of engineering from 1927 that still works beautifully.

The Big House is also a reminder that American college football operates on a scale that baffles most of the world. A university (not a professional franchise, not a national team) fills a 107,000-seat stadium eight times a year. That’s just how it works in Ann Arbor.

Penn State’s Beaver Stadium is in the middle of its own renovation story, but even before the current project, it held 106,572 fans. That puts it in a dead heat with some of the other American college giants.

What makes Beaver Stadium distinctive is the atmosphere. “White Out” games, where the entire stadium wears white, are genuinely one of the most visually striking things in all of sports. Over 100,000 people, all in white, in a stadium surrounded by nothing but central Pennsylvania farmland. It’s surreal.

The ongoing renovation is expected to reduce capacity somewhat while adding modern amenities. That’s a trend we’ll talk about more at the end of this list.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is the largest stadium in the world in 2026?
    Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, India, is the largest stadium in the world by capacity at 132,000 seats.
It is a cricket ground, not a football venue, and sits roughly 19,000 seats clear of the next-largest, Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang at 113,281. Narendra Modi Stadium opened in its current rebuilt form in 2020.

What is the largest stadium in the United States?
    Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, nicknamed 'The Big House,' is the largest stadium in the United States and the largest in the Americas at 107,601 capacity. It regularly exceeds that on game day, with an on-campus attendance record of 115,109 set against Notre Dame in 2013. It is a college football stadium, the format that dominates the upper end of US capacity rankings.

How many stadiums hold more than 100,000 people?
    Eleven stadiums have a permanent capacity above 100,000 in 2026, and Camp Nou becomes the twelfth at 105,000 once its Espai Barça expansion is complete.
Most of the 100,000-plus venues are US college football stadiums, including Michigan (107,601), Beaver (106,572), Ohio (102,780), Kyle Field (102,733), Tiger (102,321), and Neyland (101,915).

What is the largest football stadium in the world?
    Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, is the largest stadium that hosts football, at 113,281 capacity. Among club football grounds, Camp Nou in Barcelona becomes Europe's largest at approximately 105,000 once its Espai Barça expansion is finished, up from its previous 99,354.

Why is Camp Nou ranked above Michigan Stadium even though Michigan is bigger?
    We rank Camp Nou at number three on its post-expansion target of 105,000, reflecting its status as Europe's largest stadium after the Espai Barça project. By strict 2026 capacity, Michigan Stadium (107,601) is larger, and Camp Nou's current configuration is 99,354 mid-expansion.
The placement is an editorial call that weighs the expansion and football significance; a pure-capacity ranking would list Michigan ahead.

What is the largest stadium hosting the 2026 World Cup?
    AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, is the largest 2026 World Cup venue at roughly 94,000 for the tournament, using its end-zone standing-room sections. Estadio Azteca in Mexico City follows at 87,523, and MetLife Stadium, which hosts the final, runs 78,576 for the World Cup. No 2026 host venue reaches the 100,000-plus mark.
